newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Both Governor Chris Patten and Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa pledged to take action against property market speculations.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- About 27,000 potential buyers registered to buy flats in Sun Hung Kai Property's East Point City, and HK$9.5 billion has been tied up in deposits.
-- MING PAO -- Local dealers of Chinese products are planning high-profile promotion campaigns, hoping the handover would help improving the image of made-in-China products.
-- Beijing will take measures to control the building of big-scale shopping malls.
-- WEN WEI PO -- China will take further measures to encourage good-quality enterprises to take over backward ones.
-- Guangzhou will invest 11.2 billion yuan in urban construction this year. The biggest project will be the underground system.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A top tax official warned his department was gathering information on recent property transactions in order to hit speculators with taxes.
-- Sources said the price of China Eastern Airlines' initial public offer for its dual Hong Kong and New York listings would value the airline at about the same level as Cathay Pacific.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The first hi-tech H-share was about to appear, with the Shenzhen branch of China Aviation Technology Import and Export Corp planning to hive off seven hi-tech companies.
